name: reduce-motion-simple
description: REDUCE-MOTION-TOGGLE (U4, v0.35.12.4) simple rung. The control exists in the Appearance popover in SIMPLE mode (it is not flag-gated -- an accessibility preference must never be a Pro feature), it is a tri-state segmented control (System / Reduce / Full) with 44px tap targets at phone width, picking a value writes the store AND persists to `hdb_appearance`, and the value survives a reload. The observable effect is measured on the ONE animation a store-only scenario can trigger deterministically: TierChangeVeil renders `.tier-veil-bar-fill` only when motion is allowed (src/ui/loading/TierChangeVeil.tsx), so its presence/absence is a real read of `shouldReduceMotion()` rather than a read of the preference we just wrote.

steps.name: setup
steps.eval: (() => { try { localStorage.setItem('hdb_onboarded','1') } catch {}; const s = window.__store.getState(); s.endTour?.(); s.setOnboardingOpen?.(false); s.dismissLocationPrompt?.(); s.dismissChecklist?.(); s.setManualHour?.(13); s.setTimeMode?.('manual'); s.setWeather?.('clear'); s.setDeviceClass?.('capable'); s.hideLoading?.(); s.setFeatureFlag?.('interactiveDegrade', false) })()

steps.name: pin-device-class
steps.eval: (() => { const s = window.__store; s.getState().setDeviceClass('capable'); s.setState({ setDeviceClass: () => {} }) })()

steps.name: default-is-system
steps.failMessage: the tri-state must default to 'system' -- deferring to the OS is the only default that does not override a preference the user already expressed elsewhere

steps.name: open-appearance
steps.eval: (() => { const b = [...document.querySelectorAll('button')].find(b => /appearance|theme/i.test(b.getAttribute('aria-label') || b.getAttribute('title') || '')); if (!b) throw new Error('could not find the Appearance trigger in the toolbar'); b.click() })()

steps.name: control-present-in-simple
steps.eval: (() => { const labels = ['System','Reduce','Full']; const btns = [...document.querySelectorAll('button')].filter(b => labels.includes(b.textContent.trim())); if (btns.length < 3) throw new Error('the Reduce-motion tri-state (System / Reduce / Full) is not rendered in SIMPLE mode -- found ' + btns.length + ' of 3. An accessibility preference must be reachable without switching to Pro.'); const heading = /Reduce motion/i.test(document.body.textContent); if (!heading) throw new Error("the section heading 'Reduce motion' is missing (V11: the word a user scans for must appear as a LABEL, not only in the caption prose)"); window.__rmBtns = btns.map(b => ({ text: b.textContent.trim(), w: Math.round(b.getBoundingClientRect().width), h: Math.round(b.getBoundingClientRect().height) })); console.log('[probe] tri-state ' + JSON.stringify(window.__rmBtns)) })()

steps.name: persisted
steps.eval: (() => { const raw = localStorage.getItem('hdb_appearance'); if (!raw) throw new Error('nothing written to hdb_appearance'); const p = JSON.parse(raw); if (p.reduceMotion !== 'on') throw new Error('hdb_appearance.reduceMotion is ' + JSON.stringify(p.reduceMotion) + ', expected "on" -- the preference is not persisted alongside theme/modePref'); console.log('[probe] persisted ' + raw) })()

steps.name: assert-veil-suppressed
steps.eval: (() => { const n = document.querySelectorAll('.tier-veil-bar-fill').length; window.__veilUnderReduce = n; if (n !== 0) throw new Error('TierChangeVeil rendered its animated bar (' + n + ' x .tier-veil-bar-fill) while reduceMotion === "on" -- shouldReduceMotion() is not reaching this call site'); })()

steps.name: pick-full
steps.eval: (() => { const b = [...document.querySelectorAll('button')].find(b => b.textContent.trim() === 'Full'); if (!b) { window.__store.getState().setReduceMotion('off'); return } b.click() })()

steps.name: assert-veil-plays
steps.eval: (() => { const n = document.querySelectorAll('.tier-veil-bar-fill').length; if (n === 0) throw new Error('CONTROL ARM FAILED: TierChangeVeil rendered NO animated bar even with reduceMotion === "off". Without this the suppression assertion above passes vacuously (the veil may simply never render in this harness).'); console.log('[probe] veil ' + JSON.stringify({ underReduce: window.__veilUnderReduce, underFull: n })) })()

steps.name: back-to-system
steps.eval: (() => { const b = [...document.querySelectorAll('button')].find(b => b.textContent.trim() === 'System'); if (b) b.click(); else window.__store.getState().setReduceMotion('system') })()

steps.name: open-appearance-phone
steps.eval: (() => { const b = [...document.querySelectorAll('button')].find(b => /appearance/i.test(b.getAttribute('aria-label') || '')); if (b) { b.click(); return } /* On a phone the trigger lives two taps deep, inside the hamburger sheet's 'Appearance & help' accordion section (toolbar/mobile/AppearanceSection.tsx) -- the desktop toolbar button does not exist. Drive the same store action its row calls rather than hunting the sheet, which is a different feature's surface. */ const s = window.__store.getState(); if (!s.setAppearanceOpen) throw new Error('setAppearanceOpen is gone from the store -- the Appearance sheet cannot be opened on a phone'); s.setAppearanceOpen(true) })()

steps.name: phone-tap-targets
steps.eval: (() => { const labels = ['System','Reduce','Full']; const btns = [...document.querySelectorAll('button')].filter(b => labels.includes(b.textContent.trim())); if (btns.length < 3) throw new Error('the tri-state is not rendered on the phone Appearance surface -- found ' + btns.length + ' of 3'); if (!document.body.classList.contains('mobile')) throw new Error('body.mobile is not set at 390x844 -- the 44px tap-target rules live inside `body.mobile {}` under @media (max-width: 960px), so nothing below would be tested. Run this scenario with SHOT_TOUCH=1.'); /* Measure the LAYOUT box (offsetHeight), not getBoundingClientRect(). The sheet animates in with a `pop` scale keyframe, and the rect is the TRANSFORMED box -- it reads 43.1px for a button whose computed min-height is a correct 44px, i.e. 44 x 0.98. Asserting on the rect turns an entrance animation into a phantom 1px tap-target violation. offsetHeight ignores transforms and is what the 44px rule actually means. */ const rows = btns.map(b => { const r = b.getBoundingClientRect(); const cs = getComputedStyle(b); return { t: b.textContent.trim(), layoutH: b.offsetHeight, paintedH: +r.height.toFixed(1), minH: cs.minHeight, w: b.offsetWidth } }); console.log('[probe] phone-tri-state ' + JSON.stringify(rows)); const small = rows.filter(x => x.layoutH < 44); if (small.length) throw new Error('tap targets under 44px on a phone: ' + small.map(x => x.t + '=' + x.layoutH + 'px (min-height: ' + x.minH + ')').join(', ') + ' -- CLAUDE.md requires 44px under the max-width:960px media query'); const off = btns.map(b => b.getBoundingClientRect()).filter(r => r.right > 390.5 || r.left < -0.5); if (off.length) throw new Error('the tri-state overflows the 390px viewport') })()

steps.name: survives-reload
steps.failMessage: reduceMotion did not survive a reload -- it must be rehydrated from hdb_appearance like theme and modePref
